key_insight: HamGNN-NEGF uses an E(3)-equivariant GNN to predict DFT-quality Hamiltonians for large devices, enabling linear-scaling quantum transport with near-DFT fidelity.
engineering_relevance: This makes predictive transport simulations feasible for realistic nanoelectronic devices at the 10,000-atom scale, far beyond conventional DFT-NEGF limits.
method: Train on conventional DFT Hamiltonians from small structures, not expensive DFT-NEGF data.
Predict device Hamiltonians with an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network.
Combine with DFT electrode self-energies, kernel polynomial Fermi-level estimation, and recursive Green's functions for linear scaling.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on Pt-Si-Pt, doped Pt-Si:P-Pt, and Pt-molecule-Pt junctions report meV-level Hamiltonian accuracy, faithful transmission spectra, and >1000× speedups even below 500 atoms.
watch_item: The zero-bias Hamiltonian approximation is only expected to be reliable in weakly nonlinear regimes, so strong-bias transport may need additional validation.
paper_title: Linear-Scaling Quantum Transport from Machine-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonians
